title: An INCLUDE statement imbeds a group of DD statements held in a member of a JCLLIB library
shapes: BDLD jcl/BDLDINC.jcl INC010: //INC1 INCLUDE MEMBER=BDLDDDS after the EXEC, JCLLIB ORDER=(PROD.BDLD.PROCLIB)
BDLD proclib/BDLDDDS.prc: the INCLUDE group, bare DD statements (SYSPRINT, SYSUT2), no PROC or PEND
asserts: The EXEC of INC010 is one jcl_steps fact carrying includes ['BDLDDDS']. The DDs of the INCLUDE group are jcl_dds facts of the member BDLDDDS (job null, proc null, include BDLDDDS, step null): the group is a member of its own, not a procedure, and has no jcl_steps fact. At run time the group replaces the INCLUDE statement, so SYSPRINT and SYSUT2 are DDs of step INC010.

citations.quote: Identify the name of the member of a partitioned data set (PDS) or partitioned data set extended (PDSE) that contains a set of JCL statements (such as DD and OUTPUT JCL statements) called an INCLUDE group.
The INCLUDE group replaces the INCLUDE statement, and the system processes the imbedded JCL statements as part of the JCL stream.

citations.section: Chapter 19. INCLUDE statement > Location in the JCL
citations.quote: if there is a JCLLIB statement, the INCLUDE statement must follow the JCLLIB statement.

citations.section: Chapter 19. INCLUDE statement > Considerations for using INCLUDE groups
citations.quote: Do not define procedures in an INCLUDE group.
